patches/seq: A transformer reads a sequence of vectors, one per token. An image is a grid of pixels: here thirty two by thirty two, with three color values each.
patches/cut: To make it a sequence, cut it into squares of P by P pixels, the patches. Here P is eight.
patches/count: Thirty two over eight is four patches along each side, so four times four: sixteen patches, read in order like words on a page.
patches/formula: In general, an H by H image gives H over P, squared. Two hundred and twenty four pixels in patches of sixteen gives fourteen squared: one hundred and ninety six.
flatten/one: Take one patch. It is eight by eight pixels, and each pixel has three color values: eight times eight times three is one hundred and ninety two numbers.
flatten/flat: Lay them out in one row: a vector of P squared times C numbers, where C is the number of color channels.
flatten/embed: A learned linear map, a weight matrix and a bias, turns that row into a token of d numbers, the width the transformer works in. Here d is sixty four.
flatten/shared: Every patch goes through the same map, so there is one set of weights: one hundred ninety two times sixty four, plus sixty four biases. Twelve thousand three hundred and fifty two, whatever the size of the image.
flatten/conv: That is a convolution: sixty four filters of P by P, with a stride of P, so each one lands on whole patches and never overlaps.
sequence/tokens: Do that for all sixteen patches, and the image is a sequence: sixteen tokens of sixty four numbers, a sixteen by sixty four matrix.
sequence/cls: One more token goes in front: the class token. It is learned, it comes from no patch, and it is the same for every image. Now the sequence is seventeen by sixty four.
sequence/blocks: From here it is a plain transformer. Each block keeps the shape, seventeen tokens in and seventeen out, and attention lets every patch look at every other.
sequence/read: After the last block, the class token has gathered what it needs from all the patches, and a linear classifier scores it.
